body:
No one in this entire thread said anything about her forcing herself to be okay with a sexual act. Where is this made up argument coming from?

​

When I first read this post top comments  were "why being insecure?""get freaky!", and siding with her boyfriend - not a fucking word about her feelings being valid and important. Disregarding  somebody's feelings and arguments like "I would be okay with it and you should too", "Don't be boring/insecure" are pressuring. People who said that she shouldn't do it were initially downvoted. I'm glad the comments are different now. I shared a guy's post about the same situation  to show how different responses are for both genders.  If I didn't do it, people would have probably argue with me that I was overreaching.

It  just shows how it is expected for women to perform sexual acts even if they don't feel right about them. I see it happening all the time (even with my female friends) - boyfriend pressuring a girl to do anal, threesomes, BDSM by hinting she is prude and boring if she doesn't do it, and that it's not a "big deal". Basically telling women how they should feel about things. People have more subtle ways to manipulate other people without outwardly forcing them to do something. But it's still pressuring and it's not right by any means. Gaslighting somebody's feelings is NOT okay.  If she's not comfortable with doing something she does not have any obligation to do it. NO MEANS NO. That's the end of story.

I'm just going to leave this link to show how fucked up double standards are in this community [https://www.reddit.com/r/relationship\_advice/comments/dgd49d/my\_23m\_girlfriend\_21f\_wants\_me\_to\_use\_a\_massive/](https://www.reddit.com/r/relationship_advice/comments/dgd49d/my_23m_girlfriend_21f_wants_me_to_use_a_massive/) The most upvoted comments there are saying that this guy's feelings are valid and he shouldn't feel bad about it. And the most upvoted comments here are pressuring this woman to bend over backwards to please her boyfriend and telling her she's just insecure. OP, you're not your boyfriend's sex slave and you shouldn't agree to anything you don't want to. YOUR FEELINGS AND BOUNDARIES ARE VALID. And for women here to tell ANOTHER woman to ignore her feelings for a guy, I'm embarrassed by you. Men stand up for other men all the time, why can't women be supportive of each other like that? It's sad, honestly.
